summary: The lecture defines economics as the study of scarce resource allocation and divides it into microeconomics (individual decisions) and macroeconomics (aggregate variables). It describes capitalist, socialist, and communist economic systems, and identifies four sectors: private, government, household, and external. The lecture also explains factors of production, circular flow of income, stock versus flow, consumption versus capital goods, and features of a closed economy.
points: Economics studies how societies allocate scarce resources to produce and distribute goods and services.
Microeconomics analyzes individual/business decisions; macroeconomics examines aggregates like national income, employment, inflation.
Capitalist economy features private ownership of production means, free markets, minimal government role.
Socialist economy: state decides what, how, for whom to produce; examples France, Sweden.
Communist economy: state owns all means of production.
Four economic sectors: private, government, household, external.
Factors of production: land earns rent, labour earns wages, capital earns interest, entrepreneur earns profit.
Circular flow shows income, goods, services, factor payments between households, firms, government, foreign sector.
Stock measured at a point in time; flow measured over a period.
Consumption goods satisfy immediate needs; capital goods are semi-finished inputs for further production.

check.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a capitalist economy according to the lecture?
opts: State ownership of means of production
Private ownership of means of production and free market

check.q: What does the circular flow of income represent?
opts: Flow of money only between households and firms
Flow of income, goods, services, and factors between households, firms, government, and foreign sector

check.q: According to the lecture, which of the following correctly distinguishes stock from flow?
opts: Stock is measured over a period; flow at a point in time
Stock is measured at a point in time; flow over a period
Both are measured over a period
Both are measured at a point in time
